records.name: Line locality: does IAM-A's line hold region by region, not only per sample
questions: Large enough to count held error with useful precision in a typical library, small enough to see regions; it is a rule, not derived.
Does held error actually go down as tiles become more firmly held, based on what's been measured so far?

Yes, in the data reported: going from the loosest methylation band (<0.5) to the firmest (>=0.85), held error drops from about 0.0546 to about 0.0480, then 0.0429, then 0.0359, i.e. a steady fall exactly in the direction the law predicts. But this pattern is flagged as a lead rather than a confirmed or derived result.

What exact threshold decides whether a tile counts as firm or loose?

Does this test explain why held error falls region by region, or just whether it does?

Just whether it does. The test only reports counts of firm and loose tiles and their opportunities, to see if the fidelity line holds regionally as well as per sample; it doesn't by itself establish the reason for any pattern found.
